title: What Can Outlast Us? / 长存共识
scope: Five complete reader essays, Simplified and Traditional Chinese plus independently written English. One series landing page and five articles. The full technical paper remains a separate source, not an implied prerequisite.
method: Lead read all 53,625 characters of the author's Chinese source, including appendices. Three explicitly authorized subagents drafted essays 1–3 in Chinese and independent English; lead read both versions in full, wrote essays 4–5, unified scope and wording, and reviewed all five generated Traditional Chinese bodies. No translation service used.

source.verification: Fresh HTTPS fetch compared byte for byte with the author's local paper, 2026-10-26; author source not modified.

coverage.focus: Ordinary agreement versus cross-generational continuation; individual practices and emergent group relations; four proposed changes; attention versus independent succession; survivor bias; slow early accumulation is not a historical countdown.

Records and tacit practice; independent understanding versus copying; several addresses versus independent capacities; distributed resilience and shared dependencies; historically completed events versus current network capacity; archives, living continuity and new attempts distinguished.

Channels and the conditions for sustained attention, trust, self-direction and uncertainty; capacity as a supported state, not a rank or essence; interacting factors; institutional closure and delayed effects on newcomers; partial proxies; material support, rest and departure.

Utility, coercion and recognition can sustain outwardly similar continuity; mechanisms may mix and change. Durability gives neither truth nor normative legitimacy. Recognition permits questioning, conflict and exit without denying historical accountability; a common solution is not perfect permanent mutual understanding.

SAE is not exempt from its own questions; preservation, citation, reception and independent practice differ; external audit remains possible without succession. Proxies, subjective scenarios, geometric time ratios and simulations have distinct evidence limits. Negative observability results do not prove a social factor; specific failed claims must be distinguished from the fate of one project.

editorial_boundaries: Fictional archives, workshops, reading groups and dinners are illustrations, not empirical support for the model or professional repair/management advice. Historical religious, craft and civilizational classifications are not reproduced as settled facts.

Four phases and the two-factor account are the paper's proposed interpretive framework. No universal empirically established stage sequence or 5:1 historical time law is asserted; no countdown, investment recommendation, group ranking or organizational growth recipe is supplied.

The source's legacy DD mapping is not repeated. Personhood recognition is not agreement with claims or a leader, a requirement never to leave, or proof that two people have achieved complete mutual understanding. No actual group is assigned a 16DD status.

The phase-history/absorbing-state convention is attributed as a convention of the source, not used to prove that an extant social network cannot shrink, lose independent nodes or regain dependence. Archive preservation alone is not living continuity.

Capacity refers to current environmentally supported conditions, not innate worth, a personality score or civilizational hierarchy. Bibliographic output, skills assessments and institutional presence do not directly measure every aspect of the proposed capacity; no unverified current decline percentages are used.

Utility is not inherently discrediting; actual groups may mix mechanisms. Recognition does not remove material needs, guarantee resilience under all shocks, or settle normative legitimacy by longevity.

The paper's 60/30/10 scenarios are subjective internal estimates, not measured probabilities; numerical details are left in the linked source. Audit years are attributed invitations, not promises of vindication.

The SDE result is reported narrowly as the paper's own model result, with detailed setup/code/data still needed for independent checking. Its limits motivate questions but do not prove the existence or causal sufficiency of a population factor in human societies.

A project's disappearance alone cannot refute every structural claim, and survival cannot establish the whole theory. Claims need pre-specified evidence and independently disputable criteria, not post-hoc reclassification of every outcome as confirmation.
